best_for: Heavy browser users who keep dozens of tabs open and want mail, calendar, feeds and an ad blocker inside one Chromium-based browser they can rearrange.
description:
Vivaldi is a desktop web browser from Vivaldi Technologies, built on Chromium, the same base as Google Chrome. Most Chrome extensions install and work in it, so you can bring your favorites along.

Quick Commands is one search box for your tabs, bookmarks, history and the web, and it also runs browser commands by name. You can pin any website to the sidebar and view it in mobile or desktop layout. It takes screenshots of a whole page or a part of the screen, pops a video out into a floating window while you work, and shows charts of your browsing history. You can move buttons and panels where you want them, and change colors, wallpapers and how round the tab corners are.

points.title: Mail, calendar and feeds built in
points.text: Vivaldi ships with a mail client, calendar and feed reader alongside the browser. You can retire a separate mail app if your needs are simple.

points.title: Tabs you can stack and tile
points.text: Tabs can be grouped into two-level stacks, tiled side by side in one window and sorted into workspaces. There are also notes, mouse gestures and command chains for repeated tasks.

points.title: Blocking and translation included
points.text: A tracker and ad blocker is built in, and a translation tool translates whole pages. Vivaldi says it does not profile you or sell your data.

points.title: Sync is end-to-end encrypted
points.text: Sync carries your browser data between devices with end-to-end encryption, on servers Vivaldi hosts in Iceland.

points.title: Not fully open source
points.text: Vivaldi is free but not under a single open-source license. Its Chromium changes are published under BSD, and the interface is plain HTML, CSS and JavaScript that anyone can read and audit.

points.title: Every Windows option, Mac 13 and up
points.text: Windows gets 32-bit, 64-bit and ARM64 installers, each for one user or the whole machine, and this site keeps 190 Windows versions. The universal Mac build needs macOS 13 or later. macOS and Linux list only the current release here.

points.title: Linux: the Flatpak is unofficial
points.text: Vivaldi's download page offers .deb and .rpm packages for x64 and ARM64, plus the Snap Store. The Flatpak listed here is not verified on Flathub and is not among Vivaldi's own downloads.
